display.purpose: First-viewport headline, two lines, bottom-left, revealed line by line from a mask.

headline.purpose: Section headlines, two short lines with a forced break; size flexes per chapter.

title.purpose: Active service tagline; 30px for the dialog heading.

title-card.purpose: Sample-card titles, the one medium-weight body-scale role.

nav.purpose: Top-bar links and the compact CTA.

label.purpose: Chapter numbers and names, step keys, the SAMPLE tag. Never headlines or captions above headings.

wordmark.purpose: Closing NEBULYX wordmark bleeding off the bottom edge.

shadows.name: sample-lift
shadows.purpose: The only DOM shadow: sample cards in the light grid room.

shadows.name: world-light-field
shadows.purpose: Screen-blended blue light field anchored past the right edge; opacity is 1 minus world-light, so it vanishes in the light room.

shadows.name: nav-band
shadows.value: background: void or grid-room (by world-light) at 82%; backdrop-filter: blur(14px); border-bottom: 1px solid ink at 10%
shadows.purpose: Scrolled top bar; depth by translucency, not shadow.

shadows.name: tile-material
shadows.value: MeshPhysicalMaterial color #1f3dff, metalness 0, roughness 0.42, clearcoat 1, clearcoatRoughness 0.06, envMapIntensity 0.32, emissive #0a21c8 at 0.38; ACES Filmic tone mapping, exposure 0.92; key light #ffffff 1.1, rim light #5c78ff 1.6
shadows.purpose: Glossy enamel of the 3D service tiles.

shadows.name: grid-floor
shadows.value: 1.4-unit cells, line opacity 0.35, plus markers every second intersection, distance fade 4 to 46 units, curvature 0.0045, fog 14 to 48; opacity 0.9 dark, 0.55 light

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: All UI state transitions, card tilt, tag roll and service swap.

motion.name: duration-roll
motion.purpose: Chapter tag roll-up and sample-card straighten.

motion.name: line-reveal
motion.purpose: Display headline lines rising out of their masks on load.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: GSAP power3.out 0.9s, y 20px, stagger 0.06s, start top 88%, once
motion.purpose: Reveal of section copy and cards.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp 0.09; anchor scroll 1.6s; service jump 1.2s
motion.purpose: Page scroll that drives chapter progress.

motion.name: world-follow
motion.value: 1 - exp(-dt * 4.5) per frame; tile bob 0.07 units at 0.7 rad/s; pointer parallax 0.35 x, 0.2 y
motion.purpose: Tiles, camera and light easing toward chapter formations.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes line reveals, tile bob and sway, pointer parallax, card and button transitions, tag roll and service swap; formations snap.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.note: Desktop nav appears; below it the world uses phone formations, fov 52 and 55% tile spread.

narrative.overview:
Nebulyx lives inside one persistent 3D world. An endless perspective grid of fine lines and plus-shaped markers curves away to a fogged horizon, and eighteen glossy blue service tiles, each carrying one white line icon, float above it. As the visitor scrolls, the same tiles regroup per chapter: an arc across the first viewport, a ring, a row with one tile lifted forward for the active service, stations joined by a lit path for the sprint, a cluster for the work. The page never cuts to a new scene; the world keeps moving underneath flat, quiet type.

The default room is a near-black void with one soft electric-blue light field bleeding in from the right edge. For the work chapter the whole world turns into a light grid room: the background, fog and grid lines blend toward pale grey and dark ink, and every piece of chrome that reads the world-light value flips with it. Density is low. Headlines are large and light-weight, body copy is short, and the interface over the scene is thin: square containers, 2px controls, hairline borders and one blue.

The system rejects the stacked-sections agency template and the glowing-orb hero. Depth belongs to the 3D world, not to cards, gradients or glows painted on the interface.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous WebGL scene behind every section, with a flat 56px CSS grid as the no-WebGL fallback.
Glossy rounded blue tiles with a single white line icon are the recurring signature object.
One chromatic hue, Nebulyx Blue, across CTAs, active states, chapter numbers and tiles.
A dark void by default and a light grid room for the work chapter, switched by the world, not by section backgrounds.
Large, light, tightly tracked General Sans display type over minimal chrome.
One corner language: 2px on controls, square on containers, soft radius only on the 3D tiles and the logo mark.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Nebulyx Blue is the only chromatic color in the interface. There is no second accent; hierarchy comes from white, the grey steps and the blue, nothing else.

rules.name: The Two Rooms Rule
rules.body: The world has two rooms: the dark void and the light grid room. The room is changed by the world-light value blending background, fog, grid lines and interface ink together, never by painting a section background on its own.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type stays at weight 400 with negative tracking (-0.04em to -0.045em). Size carries the emphasis; weight never does. Medium (500) is reserved for card titles, nav and the wordmark.

rules.name: The Mono Is for Numbers Rule
rules.body: The mono face only marks chapter numbers, chapter names, step keys and the SAMPLE tag. It never sets a headline, a sentence or a caption above a heading.

rules.name: The World Carries Depth Rule
rules.body: Only the 3D world and the sample cards in the light room have depth. Buttons, fields, chips, the nav and the dialog stay flat at rest and on hover; state is shown by color, border and a 1px lift, never a glow.

dos: **Do** use Nebulyx Blue (#3a5bff) as the only accent, and Focus Blue (#8fa2ff) for every focus outline at 2px with a 3px offset.
**Do** keep controls at 2px corners and containers square; save rounded forms for the 3D tiles and the logo mark.
**Do** put one white line icon on each tile face, never text or a filled glyph.
**Do** label every illustrative project, mockup or diagram with the black mono SAMPLE tag.
**Do** switch to the light grid room through the world-light value so background, grid, nav and chapter tag change together.
**Do** ease state changes on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and honour reduced motion by removing line reveals, tile drift, card transitions and tag rolls.
**Do** keep the flat 56px CSS grid fallback in step with the world when WebGL is unavailable.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second accent hue, a gradient fill on interface elements, or the old cyan.
**Don't** use pill-shaped buttons or chips, or rounded cards.
**Don't** add glows or coloured box-shadows to buttons, cards or the nav; the only DOM shadow is the sample card's.
**Don't** place a centred glowing orb or blob behind headlines; the only light is the blue field anchored at the right edge.
**Don't** set kickers or eyebrow labels above headings, mono or otherwise.
**Don't** present client logos, metrics, testimonials or case studies as real proof; illustrative work is labelled SAMPLE.
**Don't** stack the page as boxed sections over a plain background; every chapter sits on the shared world.
